claims.claim: On 2026-10-29 Alexander Koch posted that customers can book Tau's humanoid cleaners on a recurring subscription for up to 3 hours per cleaning, with video at 4x speed.
Tau's booking page quotes a one-hour visit with two humanoids at $60 weekly, $80 every two weeks, $90 every four weeks and $100 one-time, with invite-only booking.
Tau's Service Terms (updated 2026-10-24) state the standard fee is $50 per humanoid per hour, normally two humanoids, i.e. $100, $200 or $300 for 1, 2 or 3 hours.
Tau's Service Terms state: the robot is not autonomous, a person is controlling it, and every cleaning is recorded with the operator watching live.
Tau's Service Terms cap liability at $2,500 per cleaning claim, license footage for model training, contain no insurance clause and require AAA arbitration in San Francisco.
Tau's Service Privacy Policy says head and wrist cameras record continuously, faces are not blurred, microphones are disabled, and video is retained indefinitely unless deletion is requested.
Koch told The Register each humanoid is jointly controlled by a human operator and AI and that the balance varies by task.
CBS reported Koch saying each Tau robot costs $50,000 to make, that cameras, networking and computers are Tau's own, and that robots will first imitate then exceed human performance.
A MarketWatch-derived summary reports Tau has about eight robots, roughly 160 paid robot-hours and nearly 100 cleanings, all teleoperated.
Hoodline reports Tau raised $2.6 million in pre-seed funding and has three engineers.
Unitree's G1 page lists about 1.32 m height, about 35 kg, about 2 kg arm payload, a 9000 mAh battery, about 2 hours runtime, and a base price of about $13.5k.
Unitree unveiled the G1 at $16,000 in May 2024.
A reseller lists the G1 battery as 46.8 V nominal and 421.2 Wh.
On 2026-07-28 the FCC added foreign-produced advanced robotic devices to the Covered List, except those granted Conditional Approval by the Department of War (DA 26-786).
Trade coverage reports Unitree authorized several products before the FCC rule and that the US was 13.3% of Unitree's 2025 revenue.
A 2025 arXiv security assessment found the Unitree G1 maintains telemetry connections to external servers sending robot state and sensor data and uses static encryption keys.
BLS May 2023 data show a median hourly wage of $16.08 and 836,230 jobs for maids and housekeeping cleaners.
IBISWorld sizes US residential cleaning services at about $18.8 billion in 2024.
Mobile ALOHA co-training raised whole-task success on wiping wine from 50% to 95% and rinsing a pan from 0% to 80%.
pi0.5 used about 400 hours of mobile-manipulator data from roughly 100 homes and cleans kitchens and bedrooms in entirely new homes.
pi*0.6 box-assembly iterations mixed 600 autonomous trials with 360 expert-intervention trials, and on-robot RL more than doubled throughput on the hardest tasks.
The HIW-500 dataset offers 500+ hours of G1 whole-body teleoperation across 12 real homes under CC BY 4.0.
1X NEO is priced at $20,000 or $499 per month with a $200 refundable deposit.
Gatsby charges a flat $150 per clean and claims the first US consumer humanoid cleaning on 2026-05-14.
Weave announced Isaac 1 at $7,999 or $449 per month with teleoperation fallback and fall 2026 deliveries.
Sunday Robotics raised a $165 million Series B at a $1.15 billion valuation in March 2026.
Weekly-subscription price per robot-hour is $60 per visit divided by two robots, i.e. $30.
assumptions: Both robots billed for the full hour

claims.claim: One-time booking price per robot-hour is $100 divided by two robots, i.e. $50.
assumptions: Both robots billed for the full hour
